$comment: Primary-source oracle — married-filing-separately cases: MFS brackets = MFJ/2, MFS senior-deduction ineligibility, the §86 lived-together zero base, the CMS MFS IRMAA schedule, and §36B PTC ineligibility. Expected values derived independently from the cited sources; never from production code.

rp-2025-32-mfs.name: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 Table 4 (§1(j)(2)(D)) — 2026 married-filing-separately ordinary brackets (statutorily MFJ / 2)
rp-2025-32-mfs.identifier: MFS 22% floor $50,400 = MFJ $100,800 / 2; 37% floor $384,350 = $768,700 / 2; MFS standard deduction $16,100 (IR-2025-103); §2.15 married age-65 additional deduction $1,650

irs-fs-2025-03.name: IRS FS-2025-03 — Working Families Tax Cuts deductions (Pub. L. 119-21 §70103 senior deduction)
irs-fs-2025-03.identifier: Deduction for Seniors: taxpayers must 'file jointly if married, to claim the deduction' — MFS is ineligible regardless of age or MAGI

usc-86c1cii.name: 26 U.S.C. §86(c)(1)(C) — MFS lived-with-spouse base amounts are zero
usc-86c1cii.identifier: Base amount is 'zero in the case of a taxpayer who is married as of the close of the taxable year ... but does not file a joint return ... and does not live apart from his spouse at all times during the taxable year'

cms-2026-mfs.name: CMS — 2026 Medicare Parts A & B Premiums and Deductibles (MFS lived-with-spouse tables)
cms-2026-mfs.identifier: MFS lived-with-spouse: <= $109,000 -> $0; > $109,000 and < $391,000 -> Part B IRMAA $446.30 / Part D $83.30 monthly; >= $391,000 -> $487.00 / $91.00. Lived-apart MFS uses the individual ladder (tier 1 $81.20 / $14.50)

irs-ptc-q9.name: IRS — Questions and answers on the Premium Tax Credit, Q9
irs-ptc-q9.identifier: MFS filers are ineligible for the PTC unless the Treas. Reg. §1.36B-2(b)(2) domestic-abuse/abandonment exception applies; the exception is never inferred (always $0)

cases.description: MFS filer age 66, ordinary $60,000: NO senior deduction (§70103 joint-return condition), married $1,650 age-65 add-on applies.
MFS under-65 filer, ordinary $70,000: crosses the MFS 22% floor at $50,400 (= MFJ $100,800 / 2 per §1(j)(2)).
§86(c)(1)(C)(ii): MFS lived-with-spouse -> $0 base amounts, 85% tier from the first dollar of provisional income.
derivation: Gross SS 20,000; other AGI 30,000 -> provisional income = 30,000 + 10,000 = 40,000 > 0 (both bases $0).

cases.description: 2026 MFS lived-with-spouse IRMAA at MAGI $120,000: the steep two-band schedule jumps straight to $446.30 B / $83.30 D monthly.
cases.tolerance: exact (statutory table lookup; annual cents = monthly * 12 * 100)
derivation: 120,000 > 109,000 and < 391,000 -> middle band: Part B 446.30/mo, Part D 83.30/mo (CMS 2025-11-14 fact sheet).

cases.description: 2026 MFS lived-apart-all-year IRMAA at MAGI $120,000: the individual ladder applies (tier 1: $81.20 B / $14.50 D monthly).
derivation: CMS/POMS HI 01101.031 table 1 covers 'married filing separately (lived apart all year)' with the individual thresholds: 120,000 in (109,000, 137,000] -> tier 1.

cases.description: §36B(c)(1)(C) / IRS PTC Q9: MFS is ineligible for the PTC; the exception is never inferred, so the modeled PTC is always $0.
derivation: IRS PTC Q&A Q9: an MFS filer may claim the PTC only under the §1.36B-2(b)(2) domestic-abuse/spousal-abandonment relief; the model records no such attestation and must emit $0 (a product decision).
The engine's eligibility gate must return false for MFS, and the PTC engine must refuse an MFS input outright.
